question: Which geometric assumptions, graph choices, hyperparameters, and statistical guarantees determine whether manifold learning yields a reliable representation rather than a visualization artifact?

key_findings.claim: The survey separates spectral one-shot embeddings from iterative attraction-repulsion embeddings and finds complementary weaknesses.
key_findings.evidence: Isomap, diffusion maps, and LTSA have stronger limiting theory but can suffer repeated eigendirections; t-SNE and UMAP often avoid that failure through repulsion yet remain more heuristic and can get trapped in local optima.

key_findings.claim: Neighborhood construction and sampling density are statistical choices, not harmless implementation details.
key_findings.evidence: Nonuniform density contracts dense regions and stretches sparse regions, while k-nearest and radius graphs converge to differently density-weighted operators. Renormalization can remove specific asymptotic biases.

key_findings.claim: Known asymptotic rates rarely specify a practical neighborhood scale.
key_findings.evidence: Rates such as h proportional to n^(-1/(d+6)) or k proportional to n^(4/(d+4)) times a log factor hide constants depending on manifold volume, curvature, and reach, and sample requirements grow exponentially with intrinsic dimension.

key_findings.claim: More samples do not make a two-dimensional embedding geometrically reproducible.
key_findings.evidence: Algorithm-dependent distortion persists under uniform dense sampling and consistent graph/Laplacian estimation. Isometric embedding may require much larger output dimension; local push-forward metrics can instead estimate and correct distortion.

anchors.section: Preserving isometry by estimating local distortion

key_findings.claim: A visually stable cluster, arm, hole, or filament is not sufficient scientific evidence.
key_findings.evidence: The survey recommends varying initialization, algorithm, parameters, perturbations, and resamples and inspecting estimated distortion before assigning meaning to a feature.

method.core_idea: Unify the geometry, algorithms, asymptotic statistics, failure modes, and scientific use of nonlinear dimensionality reduction from a practicing statistician's perspective.
method.mechanism: Define manifold and embedding targets; compare graph, eigenvector, and neighbor-embedding methods; connect graph Laplacians to limiting differential operators; then translate theory into parameter and validation guidance.
assumptions: Data concentrate near a smooth low-dimensional manifold
Local ambient distances approximate intrinsic geometry at a valid scale
Sampling density and noise can be modeled or diagnosed
The desired task determines which geometry should be preserved

techniques.role: Relates discrete graph choices to density-biased differential operators.
Tests visual features across algorithms, parameters, and resamples.
Estimates local geometry lost by an otherwise useful embedding.

evaluations.setting: illustrative manifolds including a chopped torus and molecular configurations
evaluations.metric: qualitative topology, distortion, and algorithm sensitivity
evaluations.result: standard algorithms produce different non-isometric maps and sometimes artificial crossings or clusters
evaluations.baseline: Isomap, Laplacian eigenmaps, LLE, LTSA, t-SNE, UMAP, and diffusion maps

limitations: Author-stated: manifold learning with realistic noise is largely omitted.
Author-stated: local singularities cannot yet be reliably detected or avoided.
The review is conceptual rather than a systematic literature search or benchmark.
Most guarantees require smoothness, sufficient sampling, and constants unavailable in practice.
failure_modes: A wrong intrinsic dimension collapses distant regions together.
Density variation creates apparent clusters or filaments.
Repeated eigenfunctions make a spectral embedding rank-deficient.
A heuristic neighbor embedding converges to a local optimum that looks plausible.
reusable_insights: Record graph type, scale, normalization, embedding dimension, seed, and sampling density as analysis provenance.
Validate geometry separately from the visual objective.
Use local distortion overlays and stability ensembles before scientific interpretation.
open_questions: Can local singularities be detected with finite-sample guarantees?
How should practical scales be selected when reach and curvature are unknown?
Can uncertainty-aware embeddings expose non-identifiability rather than returning one map?

competitive_landscape.title: Visualizing Data using t-SNE
competitive_landscape.difference: t-SNE optimizes neighbor probabilities to obtain useful displays; this survey explains why its repulsion is robust in practice while warning that its geometry and large-sample limit are less established.

competitive_landscape.title: UMAP: Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection for Dimension Reduction
competitive_landscape.difference: UMAP turns local fuzzy topology into a fast neighbor embedding; the survey situates it among heuristic attraction-repulsion methods and emphasizes graph-density and distortion audits.

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding How Dimension Reduction Tools Work: An Empirical Approach to Deciphering t-SNE, UMAP, TriMAP, and PaCMAP for Data Visualization
competitive_landscape.difference: Wang et al. reverse-engineer loss-design choices and propose PaCMAP; this paper supplies broader geometric and statistical foundations, including operator limits and distortion correction.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The survey explains what manifold learning does, how representative methods work, and why statistical theory matters for reliable conclusions.
novelty_assessment.evidence: It connects algorithms, graph limits, parameter rates, embedding distortions, and concrete scientific pitfalls in one treatment.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Its distinctive value is not a new algorithm but a rare bridge between asymptotic geometry and operational skepticism about popular visualizations.

reviewer_notes: Read all 33 extracted pages, with a second pass over algorithm taxonomy, statistical bias, scale choice, distortion, visualization warnings, and omitted topics. Competitor records were checked on primary arXiv/JMLR pages.
